subject: Streaming gating & burst fallback action plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Park <ellis@waveforms.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming gating & burst fallback action plan

Hi Ellis — thanks again for the product deep-dive earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the SLO verification and autoscale playbook: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Critical flow is 1:1 streaming sessions (audio transcription) with real-time token outputs.
- Typical steady concurrency ~120 sessions, peak bursts up to 1,800 concurrent sessions for up to ~10 minutes during end-of-day ingestion.
- Required latency SLOs: First-stream-byte (FSB) <= 250ms P99, ongoing per-token steady-state latency < 80ms P95.
- Failure tolerance: degrade to lower-quality model if warm pool not available; queueing acceptable up to 30s for burst tail.

Clarifying questions we need from you to finalize the test plan:
1) Can you share a representative per-session token emission rate (tokens/sec) during peaks? (Sophie, if you have the CSV from yesterday, please paste.)
2) Are sessions long-lived (minutes) or short-lived (tens of seconds) on average?
3) Do you require strict ordering across tokens or can we stream in micro-batches?

Proposed immediate next steps from Redwood: 
- Run a 30-minute peak simulation (we'll use the WaveForms CSV you shared) with a warm pool configured and measure scale-up time, queue depth, and FSB P99.
- Acceptance gates: FSB P99 <= 250ms during warm-pool-backed traffic; warm-pool cold-start scale-up <= 45s to reach target capacity for 1,800 sessions; queue tail < 30s.
- Deliverable: test report + suggested warm-pool sizing and fallback config.

I've attached the SLO matrix template and a quick CSV stub for the load profile you mentioned. If the numbers above are off, tell us which value to adjust and we'll update the runbook.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Ellis Park <ellis@waveforms.com>

Cc: Sophie Lin <sophie@waveforms.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming gating & burst fallback action plan

Vanessa — thanks for the write-up and for capturing the gates. Quick answers inline and attaching our real production extract: 

On your questions:
1) Tokens/sec: average during peaks ~18 tokens/sec per session (some longer sessions spike to 45 tokens/sec for ~30s). CSV attached (waveforms_load_profile_v2.csv).
2) Session duration: median 4.2 minutes, 90th percentile ~11 minutes.
3) Ordering: strict ordering is required, we cannot micro-batch across sessions, but batching tokens within a session by 2-4 tokens is acceptable (client can buffer).

One constraint: absolute maximum queueing we can tolerate is 40s in exceptional events (we prefer <30s but can extend for infra-ledging with user notification).

Also, we have a regulatory requirement to avoid exposing intermediary tokens to a lower-tier model for transcription; fallback model must meet same redaction assurance (so functionally the same model family or a certified equivalent).

Ellis
Ellis Park
Director of Platform Engineering, WaveForms Inc.
ellis@waveforms.com | +1 212-555-0090

Attachment: waveforms_load_profile_v2.csv (full)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Park <ellis@waveforms.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming gating & burst fallback action plan

Thanks Ellis — the numbers are very helpful. Based on the profile, proposed Redwood test plan and acceptance criteria: 

Test plan (30-min peak run + 10-min cool-down):
- Baseline steady: 120 concurrent sessions for 10m to validate latency and KV-cache warm state.
- Burst ramp: linear ramp to 1,800 concurrent sessions over 90s, hold for 10m, then decay.
- Token emission per session: use median 18 tps with 10% of sessions at 40–45 tps to model spikes.
- Streaming constraints: preserve token ordering; allow intra-session micro-batching of 2–3 tokens where runtime supports it.

Acceptance gates (pass/fail):
- FSB P99 <= 250ms for warm-backed requests.
- Per-token P95 <= 80ms during steady; allow up to P95=140ms during the 90s ramp window.
- Warm-pool cold-start to reach capacity for extra 1,680 sessions <= 45s measured from scaling trigger.
- Backlog queue depth: 95th percentile < 20s, absolute max < 40s.
- Fallback model: must be on our verified equivalent list; will require SOC/compliance sign-off (Ellis please confirm allowed fallback tags).

Operational checks we'll include:
- KV cache priming and hit-rate breakdown per model shard.
- Per-route cost impact estimate for warm-pool vs burst provisioning.
- Streaming jitter and partial-token retransmit behavior.

Proposed dates: run the tests next Tuesday (Dec 7) 09:00–10:00 PT with a pre-run warmup window. Rishi — can your team instrument the harness and collect trace spans for P99 calculation?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: slo-matrix.xlsx (filled), proposed-test-steps.md

Subject: Re: Streaming gating & burst fallback action plan

Marissa — confirmed, we can run the harness and collect the spans. Notes from SRE perspective: 

Instrumentation and veriﬁcation items:
- We'll instrument FSB as the timestamp for first byte emitted by the runtime (not client ack). Traces will include model selection, KV cache hit flag, and queue time.
- Scale trigger will be defined by sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for 15s across the serving pool or queue depth > 60 requests for 10s (we'll record both).
- Warm-pool policy: pre-warm 200 instances to start (configurable), ramp policy to add up to +1,500 within 45s via parallel provisioning lanes.
- Fallback test: we will simulate fallback invocation for 5% of requests during the tail to ensure behavior and audit logs meet compliance.

I'll post the harness link and an instrumentation checklist by EOD. Vanessa — can you confirm the legal/compliance contact so we can pre-clear fallback model tags?

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
